items.title: 68002_Benny Waters oral history interview
items.q: That's what, that's the character of his playing from Gerry Mulligan, and they both were great.

ctx.x: Yeah, well yeah, and have you ever heard another guy named Benny H-, no, I think that's from Philadelphia. Well, those guys mostly - there's one in Paris right now by the name Mule, got the same thing. They get a straight tone, that's where some of the smartest stuff is coming in with the straight tone, which sounds so bad sometimes. But no vibrato, no coloring a note, just a 'Dooooo' - 'cause they didn't know how to

play that saxophone, that's like when it's a new instrument. It's clarinet that people raise hell with, but not the saxophone. And so Carney, as he told me, the reason that he wanted to make a change from the Conservatory, because he didn't - he would listen to other guys play in the dance bands and so forth with that very beautiful sound, you know, see, and he didn't have it. See what I mean? So he wanted to come, he wanted to know how to get that vibrato, that's what I taught him and how to breath, how to make…

mean, that's why they can't get those low notes, listen to it. I'm not, of course I'm more advanced now, like I take, I can do it, Buddy Tate can, Coleman could, naturally because he's the father of all that stuff, see. Guys like Don Byas were perfect on it, Charlie Ventura mastered it, I know many. But I mean, that's where the secret is, you have to know how to do it, and that's what he was payin' for. Understand what I mean?
